# Infant Formula, Powder (Non-Soy)

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="infant-formula-powder-non-soy-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="infant-formula-powder-non-soy-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="infant-formula-powder-non-soy-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Non-soy powdered infant formula in the HMI library has 1,911 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, <p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of infant formula, powder (non-soy), group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>2 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Infant Formula, Powder (Non-Soy) FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-non-soy-powdered-infant-formula" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-non-soy-powdered-infant-formula" data-question="What heavy metals are found in non-soy powdered infant formula?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in non-soy powdered infant formula?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, B, Ba, Ca, I, K, Li, Mg, Mo, Na, P and Sr in non-soy powdered infant formula, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/almeida2022-brazil-infant-formula-toxic-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-origins-or-products-of-non-soy-powdered-infant-formula-measured-lowest" data-anchor="which-origins-or-products-of-non-soy-powdered-infant-formula-measured-lowest" data-question="Which origins or products of non-soy powdered infant formula measured lowest?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which origins or products of non-soy powdered infant formula measured lowest?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In one study, lead across 13 groups of non-soy powdered infant formula ranged from 28.7 µg/kg (milk-based formula composite IMF13, purchased in Pakistan) to 97 µg/kg (milk-based formula composite IMF6, purchased in Pakistan); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kazi2009-toxic-elements-in-infant-formulae|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tasneem G. Kazi, Nusrat Jalbani, Jameel A. Baig, Hassan I. Afridi, Ghulam A. Kandhro, Mohammad B. Arain, Mohammad K. Jamali, Abdul Q. Shah · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kazi2009-toxic-elements-in-infant-formulae">Determination of toxic elements in infant formulae by using electrothermal atomic absorption spectrometer</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Chemical Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kazi2009-toxic-elements-in-infant-formulae">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 12 groups of non-soy powdered infant formula ranged from 50 µg/kg (retail product M5, Tenerife pharmacies) to 90 µg/kg (retail product M1, Tenerife pharmacies); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/dominguez2017-tenerife-infant-formula-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Domínguez A, Paz S, Rubio C, Gutiérrez Á, González-Weller D, Revert C, Hardisson A · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dominguez2017-tenerife-infant-formula-metals">Essential and Toxic Metals in Infant Formula from the European Community</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Open Access Journal of Toxicology 2(2):555585</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dominguez2017-tenerife-infant-formula-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-non-soy-powdered-infant-formula-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-non-soy-powdered-infant-formula-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in non-soy powdered infant formula is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in non-soy powdered infant formula is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 5 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/jackson2012-arsenic-speciation-infant-formulas-first-foods|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Brian P. Jackson, Vivien F. Taylor, Tracy Punshon, Kathryn L. Cottingham · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jackson2012-arsenic-speciation-infant-formulas-first-foods">Arsenic concentration and speciation in infant formulas and first foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Pure and Applied Chemistry, Vol. 84, No. 2, pp. 215-223</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jackson2012-arsenic-speciation-infant-formulas-first-foods">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2024-risk-assessment-iAs-update|13]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA CONTAM Panel, Schrenk D, Bignami M, Bodin L, Chipman JK, del Mazo J, Grasl-Kraupp B, Hogstrand C, Hoogenboom R, Leblanc JC, Nebbia CS, Nielsen E, Ntzani E, Petersen A, Sand S, Vleminckx C, Wallace H, Barregård L, Benford D, Broberg K, Dogliotti E, Fletcher T, Rylander L, Cortiñas Abrahantes J, Gómez Ruiz JA, Steinkellner H, Tauriainen T, Schwerdtle T · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2024-risk-assessment-iAs-update">Update of the risk assessment of inorganic arsenic in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2024-risk-assessment-iAs-update">Read source
